RAJYA SABHA

MR. CHAIRMAN in the Chair.

OBITUARY REFERENCE 
MR. DEPUTY CHAIRMAN: Hon'ble Members, I refer with profound sorrow to the 
passing away of Shri Chandra Shekhar, a sitting Member of the Lok Sabha and a former 
Prime Minister of India and a former Member of this House, on the 8th July, 2007, 
following prolonged illness at the age of 81 years. 
Shri Chandra Shekhar was born in July, 1927 at Ibrahimpatti in Ballia district of 
Uttar Pradesh and had his education at Allahabad University. 
An agriculturist and a social worker, Shri Chandra Sekhar was cl osely associated 
with Acharya Narendra Dev. Shri Chandra Shekhar was known for his courage of 
conviction and principles. A socialist by conviction he was associated with various 
socialist movements in the country and was committed to people's welfare. He w as also 
associated with various social institutions and took keen interest in the field of primary 
education and health services. He undertook Padayatra from Kanyakumari to Rajghat 
and established Bharat Yatra centres in various States to train the social and political 
workers for grassroot work and mass education. 
He was President of the Janata Party from the year 1977 to 1978 and was leader of 
the Samajwadi Janata Party (Rashtriya) Parliamentary Party. He was Founder-Editor and 
Chairman of the Editorial Advisory Board of 'Young Indian'. 
The distinguished legislative career of Shri Chandra Shekhar, which spanned over 
four decades, commenced with the membership of this august House. He represented 
the State of Uttar Pradesh in this House for three terms from  April, 1962 to April, 1968; 
April, 1968 to April, 1974 and, again, from April, 1974 to March, 1977. He was also a 
Member of the Sixth, Seventh, Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh, Twelfth, Thirteenth and 
Fourteenth Lok Sabha. Known for his oratorical skills, he was a lways heard with rapt 
attention in the House. Because of his exemplary parliamentary performance, the best 
Parliamentarian Award was conferred on him in the year 1995. 
Shri Chandra Shekhar had the distinction of serving as the Prime Minster of India 
form 1990 to 1991. 
In the passing away of Shri Chandra Shekhar, the country has lost an eminent 
Parliamentarian, a veteran socialist leader, an able administrator and a champion of the 
downtrodden sections of the society. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect to 
the memory of the departed. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)
